Summary: enterprise evaluation focused on Dedicated capacity + strict latency SLO alignment. Primary driver is chat + reranking for a high-frequency trading analytics UI (low tail latency). They want clear, measurable guarantees for p50/p95/p99 across streaming vs non-streaming paths and a reproducible measurement method (server-side vs client-side).

Recent timeline (short bullets):
- 2026-02-20: discovery call (Avery) — confirmed use-cases and sensitive data residency needs.
- 2026-02-27: architecture deep-dive with Infra + Security (Ravi) — walked through VPC options, KMS, audit logging.
- 2026-03-02: metrics & SLO sync (internal + Redwood) — asked for breakdown: runtime vs network vs client overhead.
- 2026-03-05: shared Redwood Dedicated sizing draft (drive link).

Use-case / requirements (shorthand):
- Workload: low-latency conversational UI + reranking for trade alerts. Mixed short-turn chat (avg tokens 40) + occasional long summaries (avg tokens 800).
- Targets: streaming chat p50 < 80ms, p95 < 200ms, p99 < 350ms (client-observed preferred); non-streaming generation p50 < 250ms, p95 < 450ms, p99 < 600ms for typical short requests. For long summaries allow higher absolute time but strict tokens/sec throughput SLO.
- Throughput: baseline 400 concurrent users (~120 qps short requests), burst capacity to 1200 concurrent (autoscale/burst).
- Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to commit reserved GPU capacity if tail guarantees reduce effective cost.
- Model prefs: open Llama-family variants + evaluation of quantized variants; want fallback to smaller model for overload with graceful degradation.
- Routing: prefer region-aware routing (na primary) and policy to route to dedicated first, fallback to hosted in emergency.

Measurement alignment notes (explicit asks):
- Need clear definition: p50/p95/p99 measured on server-side end-to-end (Redwood runtime excluding client proxies) AND client-side (end-to-end at browser/service) with mapping between the two.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: want separate SLOs. For streaming measure time-to-first-token + time-to-final-token; p95 on time-to-first-token is critical.
- Client-side timing: they observe ~50-80ms reproducible proxy overhead; ask Redwood to provide instrumentation hooks or SDK timers and a canonical trace layout (request start, routing, model generation, network egress).
- Measurement windows: 5m and 1h rolling windows with SLO burn policies; require p99 computed over 30-day window for SLA evaluation.
- Test harness: will run replay load against POC endpoint (Firecracker scripted) — need token accounting and cold-start guidance.

Reserved GPU planning feedback:
- Initial ask: 4x A100/A10-equivalent reserved with ability to burst to 8 for market open spikes.
- Expected steady-state throughput target: ~1k tokens/sec per GPU for short-chat optimized kernel; need Redwood to validate with their kernel/profile numbers.
- Autoscale policy: prefer instant burst (seconds) rather than minutes; discuss warm pool and KV cache prewarming.

SLA negotiations / commercial asks:
- Financial credits for sustained p99 breaches during business hours (US market open).
- Clear escalation path + 2hr response target for Sev1.
- Data residency + audit log retention 7 years (legal ask).

Quotes / paraphrases from VIPs:
- CTO: "We can tolerate occasional slowdowns, not sustained tail events — p99 matters more than average."
- Head of Infra: "If Redwood can show reproducible p99 numbers at scale we will move to a 12-month reserved commit."
- Product lead: "Need instrumentation we can ship in front of users to separate client overhead."

POC plan / next steps (concrete):

- Redwood to provide recommended kernel/profile numbers and a deterministic load script by 2026-03-14.
